merger_name: Veritas Capital Fund Management – Trinity Consultants

anzsic_codes.name: Management Advice and Related Consulting Services

merger_description:
Funds managed (directly or indirectly) by Veritas Capital Fund Management, L.L.C. (**Veritas**), through Project Evergreen Buyer, Inc., propose to indirectly acquire control of Lone Star Holdco, Inc. and its subsidiaries (**Trinity Consultants**) (the **Acquisition**).

Veritas is a private equity fund adviser incorporated and based in the United States. It invests in companies that provide products, software, and services, primarily technology and technology-enabled solutions, to government and commercial customers worldwide.

Trinity Consultants is an environmental health and safety consulting firm based in the United States. It supplies a range of strategic, advisory and technical consulting to its clients including environmental consulting, air quality compliance, ecological services and life sciences regulatory support. In Australia, Trinity Consultants supplies noise quality and acoustics services, air quality services, and water quality services.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided by the applicant, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is limited horizontal overlap between Veritas (and its
portfolio companies, as well as the BGIS Group) and Trinity
Consultants in the supply of environmental consulting,
monitoring, and advisory services in Australia
b. there are alternative suppliers of environmental consulting,
monitoring, and advisory services in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
